In the World Student Games, we were represented by Chris Lambert (won gold in the 100 m), Matt Douglas (won silver in the 400m hurdles and bronze in the 4x400 m relay), Goldie Sayers and Michelle Carey.
In the women's long relay the Belgrave squad pipped Sale thanks to a resounding second leg by Michelle Carey timed in the low 53's. And so to the last event the men's long relay with the trophy ours.

Michelle Carey, who has been in top form recently, was a clear winner in the 400 A race and helped the 4 x 100m relay to second place. In this race Andrea Abrams, now 32, answering a late call-up to help the team out, showed no signs of rustiness and also took second place in the B jump with over 5 metres.

The 400m heats saw a Belgrave 1-2 in heat two as Tim Benjamin and David Gillick easily had the measure of the rest of the field. Michelle Carey placed 5th in her 400m hurdles heat. Men. 100m: Round 1. 1h4 D Chambers 10.24/1.3.
A double win came in the 200m where Michelle Carey had a 5 metre advantage in the A race but Jennifer Culley’s B victory was very much closer, with the first two recording the same time.
The Centenary Cup will be engraved with the name of Michelle Carey for her winning performance of 56.31 seconds in the 400 metre hurdles at the Loughborough European Athletics Permit Meeting.
The Tommy Green Cup for the best men’s performance went to Phillips Idowu for his Commonwealth Games triple jump win and the Centenary Cup for women went to 400 metre hurdler Michelle Carey.
